question: Why is sharps safety considered essential for nursing students in healthcare settings?

options.B: It protects nurses, patients, and colleagues from preventable injuries and infections.
options.C: It reduces the cost of purchasing medical equipment.
options.D: It is only required for senior nursing officers.

explanation: Sharps safety is crucial because proper handling and disposal protect healthcare workers, patients, and colleagues from accidental injuries and potential infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is a primary factor that heightens the risk of accidental sharps exposure in clinical environments?

options.C: Hurried disposal or bypassing safety devices

explanation: The risk of accidental exposure increases during high-stress procedures, hurried disposal, or when safety devices are bypassed. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which of the following items is classified as a sharp in clinical practice?

options.B: Disposable plastic syringe bodies without needles

explanation: Hypodermic needles and suture needles are classic examples of sharps because they have sharp points capable of puncturing the skin. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why must broken glass ampoules and capillary tubes be disposed of as sharps?

options.A: Because they are made of glass and can cause lacerations and cuts
options.C: Because they must be recycled immediately
options.D: Because they are classified as general municipal waste

explanation: Broken glass ampoules and capillary tubes pose a laceration hazard and are therefore classified and treated as sharps. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which of the following are the primary bloodborne pathogens transmitted through needle-stick injuries?

options.B: HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C

explanation: The most concerning bloodborne pathogens transmitted by contaminated sharps are HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h3)

question: What factor influences the transmission risk of a bloodborne pathogen following a needle-stick injury?

options.A: The color of the syringe barrel
options.B: The brand name of the needle
options.C: The depth of the injury and whether the needle was hollow with visible blood
options.D: The time of day the procedure was performed

explanation: Transmission risk depends on several factors, including the depth of the injury, needle gauge, and whether the needle contained visible blood from the source patient. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary reason why two-handed recapping of needles is strongly discouraged?

options.A: It wastes too much time during clinical shifts.
options.B: It is the leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries.
options.C: It dulls the sharp point of the needle.

explanation: Two-handed recapping is strongly discouraged because it is the leading cause of accidental puncture wounds among healthcare personnel. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which safe technique should be used if a needle must be recapped for a specific clinical necessity?

options.A: Holding the cap with one hand and pushing the needle in with the other hand directly
options.B: Using a one-handed scoop technique or a mechanical device holder
options.C: Asking a colleague to hold the cap between their fingers
options.D: Using your teeth to stabilize the needle cap

explanation: If recapping is unavoidable, nurses must use a one-handed scoop technique or a mechanical device holder to prevent accidental finger punctures. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h4)

question: What are the key structural requirements of an approved sharps container?

options.A: It must be transparent and made of soft cardboard.
options.B: It must be puncture-resistant, leak-proof, and equipped with a secure lid.
options.C: It must be biodegradable and open at the top.
options.D: It must be washed and reused between patients.

explanation: Approved sharps containers must be puncture-resistant, leak-proof on the sides and bottom, and feature a secure lid to prevent accidental exposures. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h5)

question: Up to what level should a sharps container be filled before it is sealed and replaced?

options.A: Completely packed to the very brim
options.B: Up to the indicated fill line, generally about three-quarters (3/4) full
options.C: Only one-quarter (1/4) full to ensure constant replacement
options.D: Halfway, regardless of the manufacturer line

explanation: Sharps containers must never be overfilled; they should be sealed and replaced when they reach the fill line, which is usually about three-quarters full. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h5)

question: What action must be taken once a sharps container reaches the recommended fill line?

options.A: Empty the contents into a larger trash bag to reuse the container.
options.B: Compress the contents downward to make more room.
options.C: Securely close and lock the lid according to manufacturer instructions.
options.D: Leave the lid open until the end of the shift.

explanation: Once a sharps container reaches the fill line, it must be securely closed and locked permanently to prevent access to the contents. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the final method of destruction typically used for sealed sharps containers in healthcare waste management?
explanation: Sealed sharps containers are sent for incineration or final authorized destruction to completely neutralize biological hazards. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h6)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Suck the wound vigorously to extract contaminated blood.
options.B: Scrub the puncture site with a harsh brush and antiseptic.
options.C: Wash the puncture wound gently with soap and running water.
options.D: Cover the wound tightly without washing to trap the blood.

explanation: The immediate first-aid response is to wash the puncture wound gently with soap and running water while encouraging mild bleeding. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why is timely reporting of a needle-stick injury critical for the healthcare worker?

options.B: To initiate timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and baseline testing
options.C: To replace the lost needle on the tray
options.D: To determine who pays for the medical supplies

explanation: Timely reporting is crucial because post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and baseline testing must be started quickly to maximize effectiveness against bloodborne pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which Nigerian regulatory body emphasizes infection prevention and control as a core competency in nursing education?

options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) sets educational standards that incorporate infection prevention and control into nursing training. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is the purpose of institutional SOPs regarding sharps disposal in healthcare facilities?

options.A: To ensure compliance with national guidelines on waste segregation and safe disposal
options.B: To increase the administrative paperwork for student nurses
options.C: To restrict the use of disposable needles in wards
options.D: To reduce the number of patients admitted to the hospital

explanation: Institutional SOPs ensure that facilities comply with national guidelines regarding proper waste segregation, safety protocols, and safe disposal methods. [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h8)
